newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MCCOIST ON VERGE OF ANOTHER RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MCCOIST ON VERGE OF ANOTHER RECORD.

text.p: Rangers striker Ally McCoist could set yet another goalscoring record on Thursday in one of the most crucial derbies against Celtic of the past decade.

The 34-year-old Rangers striker, who made his debut 17 seasons ago, is just one short of equalling Gordon Wallace's post-war Scottish League scoring record of 264 goals. If cup matches and internationals are included, McCoist has scored 352 first class goals in all games.
Wallace, now on the backroom staff at Dundee United, achieved his total in a lengthy career with Montrose, Raith Rovers, Dundee United and Dundee.

He said: "It is only a matter of time before Ally overtakes me but it won't bother me. Ally is a marvellous ambassador for the game and the sheer enjoyment he gets from scoring a goal shows in his face."
McCoist's sense of occasion will surely be sharpened for Thursday's meeting with Celtic at Parkhead, with the match being screened live to millions of viewers all over Britain on satellite TV.

Celtic go into the game top of the table for the first time in 14 months with an advantage of one goal over Rangers who, this season are bidding to equal their arch-rivals' run of nine successive championships set between 1966 and 1974.

McCoist scored 22 Scottish League goals for his first club St Johnstone and then hit his 241st premier division goal for Rangers in a 2-2 draw at Raith Rovers 10 days ago. He is the highest goalscorer in Rangers history and is also the highest scorer in the history of the Scottish premier division which was introduced in 1975.
McCoist could feature for a Rangers side that will definitely be without Alan McLaren, Gordon Durie and Stuart McCall and there are still question marks over goalkeeper Andy Goram and Brian Laudrup.
Celtic are expected to have Pierre Van Hooydonk and Andreas Thom back, while Tommy Burns will probably pitch goalkeeper Stewart Kerr into his Old Firm debut.
